summary.text: If your MediSave is depleted, use family MediSave and apply for Government assistance schemes. MediFund and ComCare may also help.

details.heading: Why the $5,000 balance exists
details.body: The minimum MediSave Account balance under MediSave Care is intended to help people keep some savings for healthcare bills.

steps.name: Spouse's MediSave
steps.text: For long-term care withdrawals, tap on your spouse's MediSave.

steps.name: Family MediSave
steps.text: For other healthcare treatments, tap on your family members' MediSave.

steps.name: Government assistance
steps.text: Apply for other forms of assistance, such as ElderFund or Home Caregiving Grant, to meet your long-term care costs.

steps.name: Other support
steps.text: If you still cannot pay after Government subsidies and other support, consider MediFund and ComCare.

sources.page_title: What if I have insufficient MediSave balances for my healthcare and long-term care expenses?

quotes.text: If you have depleted your MediSave account, you may tap on your spouse's MediSave for long-term care withdrawals, and your family members' MediSave for your other healthcare treatments.
you may tap on your spouse's MediSave for long-term care withdrawals
your family members' MediSave for your other healthcare treatments
You may also apply for other forms of assistance such as means-tested Government assistance schemes (ElderFund, Home Caregiving Grant) to meet your long-term care costs needs.
If you are still unable to pay for your care even after Government subsidies and other means of support, there are other forms of assistance such as MediFund and ComCare.
The minimum MediSave Account balance of $5,000 under MediSave Care is carefully set to help individuals maintain some savings to pay for for their healthcare bills.
